record.original_question: For Wigner distribution deconvolution with symmetric or more general windows whose ambiguity factors may vanish, what bandlimit assumptions on the unknown signal are sufficient to ensure unique recovery, and more generally what quantitative relationship links the size and location of the vanishing factors |F[w · S_xi w]_x| to the band-limitedness of the signal?

evidence.quote: Question 8.4. Which band limit has to be assumed to guarantee unique recovery for symmetric windows and, more generally, what is the quantitative relation between vanishing |F [w ˝ Sξw]x| and band-limited f in terms of WDD?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be an unknown signal and let $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a known window. For $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^d$, let $S_\xi$ denote the modulation/shift operator and define the windowed correlations $[w \cdot S_\xi w]_x = \overline{w(x)}\, w(x+\xi)$ (the window's ambiguity factor at shift $\xi$, evaluated at $x$). The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) of $f$ with window $w$ is
\[ V_w f(x,\omega) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(t)\,\overline{w(t-x)}\, e^{-2\pi i \omega \cdot t}\, dt, \]
and its spectrogram is $|V_w f|^2$. Wigner Distribution Deconvolution (WDD) recovers $f$ (up to a global phase) from $|V_w f|^2$ by inverting, frequency-by-frequency, multiplication by the window ambiguity function $A_w(\xi,\eta) = \mathcal{F}_x[\,\overline{w(\cdot)}\, w(\cdot+\xi)\,](\eta)$. Recovery fails at frequencies where $A_w$ vanishes.

Problem. 
(a) Determine a sufficient bandlimit hypothesis on $f$ (i.e., a condition of the form $\operatorname{supp}\widehat{f} \subseteq \Omega$ for some explicit set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$) which, in the case of a symmetric window $w$ (so that $A_w$ may have non-trivial zero sets), guarantees that $f$ is uniquely determined (up to a global phase) by its spectrogram $|V_w f|^2$ via the WDD procedure.

(b) More generally, for an arbitrary window $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, establish a quantitative relationship between the size and location of the zero set $Z_w = \{(\xi,\eta) : A_w(\xi,\eta) = 0\}$ (where $A_w(\xi,\eta) = \big|\mathcal{F}[w \cdot S_\xi w]_x(\eta)\big|$ vanishes) and the band-limitedness of $f$ that suffices for unique recovery of $f$ from $|V_w f|^2$ through WDD.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific question relating zero sets of the window ambiguity function to bandlimit hypotheses guaranteeing unique recovery via Wigner Distribution Deconvolution. Existing WDD uniqueness results address either non-vanishing ambiguity (generic windows) or specific discrete/aliased settings, and the symmetric-window case with vanishing ambiguity factors remains posed as an open question with no quantitative answer found.

status_evidence.title: Inverting spectrogram measurements via aliased Wigner distribution deconvolution
status_evidence.snippet: Uniqueness results in WDD typically require non-vanishing window ambiguity; deals with discrete/aliased setting and bandlimited signals.
status_evidence.claim: WDD-based uniqueness theorems known so far rely on non-vanishing ambiguity factors or specific discrete/bandlimited settings, leaving the symmetric/vanishing case unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Background Removal for Ptychography via Wigner Distribution Deconvolution
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses WDD recovery procedures but does not address the symmetric-window/vanishing-ambiguity uniqueness question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent WDD literature does not provide the quantitative bandlimit-vs-vanishing relationship asked for.
